tasks.prompt: Review this application SQL built by string concatenation: SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON o.id = i.order_id WHERE YEAR(o.created_at) = 2024 AND o.customer_id = ' + userInput + ' (quotes glued around userInput). PostgreSQL; indexes exist on orders(created_at) and orders(customer_id). Goal: list line items for one customer in 2024.
criteria: flags string concatenation / SQL injection risk
flags non-sargable YEAR(created_at) (or equivalent) vs range filter
flags SELECT * or join grain issues for the stated goal
provides a parameterized rewritten query using a date range

tasks.prompt: This query returns inflated revenue: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_tags t ON o.id = t.order_id WHERE t.tag = 'vip' GROUP BY c.name. Some orders have multiple vip-related tags.
criteria: proposes a correct rewrite (e.g. pre-aggregate, EXISTS, or DISTINCT order ids)

tasks.prompt: Review before prod: DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM users WHERE last_login < '2020-01-01'. MySQL. Typo: missing closing parenthesis may or may not be present — focus on safety of the delete.
criteria: treats unconstrained or broad DELETE risk seriously
recommends transaction, SELECT preview, or LIMIT/batching strategy
mentions verifying the subquery predicate before delete
